equation_request.abstract: The effects of imperfect gate operations in implementation of Shor's prime factorization algorithm are investigated. The gate imperfections may be classified into three categories: the systematic error, the random error, and the one with combined errors. It is found that Shor's algorithm is robust against the systematic errors but is vulnerable to the random errors. Error threshold is given to the algorithm for a given number N to be factorized.

specification.problem: Model how imperfect gate operations (systematic, random, combined errors) affect the success of Shor's factoring algorithm for a number N. The abstract gives only qualitative conclusions, so only a generic background error model on a tiny instance can be reconstructed.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single tiny instance (assumed N=15, a=7) of the order-finding core with an assumed rotation-angle error model on the controlled-phase gates of the QFT. The paper's actual error models, threshold formula, and numerical results are outside scope and not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: Multiplicative order of a modulo N
Systematic angle error, same for all gates
Random angle error of gate j, e.g. zero-mean with variance \sigma^2

equations.label: Order definition
equations.description: Order finding target of Shor's algorithm.
equations.justification: Standard Shor background; the abstract names the algorithm only.

equations.label: Ideal output state before measurement
equations.description: State after modular exponentiation and ideal QFT on the counting register.
assumptions: Register ordering: counting register first, work register second; integers in binary, MSB first

equations.label: Perturbed gate model
equations.description: Assumed model: systematic error adds constant epsilon; random error adds independent noise delta_j; combined has both.
equations.justification: The abstract names the three error categories but gives no parametrization; this is a proposed model.
assumptions: Errors act on controlled-phase angles of the QFT

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of measuring a counting value that yields r by continued fractions, under the perturbed gates.
equations.justification: Proposed figure of merit to compare robustness; the paper's own metric is unknown.
assumptions: Threshold defined as the error level where P_succ drops below a chosen value

equations.label: Factor extraction
equations.description: Nontrivial factors from an even order r with a^{r/2} not congruent to -1 mod N.

registers.name: counting
registers.role: Phase estimation register measured after QFT

registers.name: work
registers.role: Holds a^x mod N for N=15

specification.initial_state: Counting register in |0>^{t} then Hadamards to uniform superposition; work register |1>.

steps.description: Prepare uniform superposition on the counting register and set the work register to |1>.
Apply controlled modular exponentiation (ideal) to get sum_x |x>|a^x mod N>.
Apply the QFT with perturbed controlled-phase angles according to the assumed error model.
Measure the counting register and evaluate the success probability over error parameters to find a threshold.
Recover r by continued fractions and compute factors.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the counting register.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Continued-fraction expansion of y/Q to get r, then gcd computation for factors (eq_5).
assumptions: N=15, a=7 (r=4), t=8 chosen as the tiny instance
Errors are confined to QFT phase gates; modular exponentiation assumed ideal
The error model and success metric are proposals, not from the abstract
